question: In the Mallampati classification, a Class III view shows which of the following on oropharyngeal inspection?

answers.text: Soft palate, fauces, uvula, and tonsillar pillars all visible

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes Mallampati Class I — the best view, predicting easy intubation.

answers.text: Soft palate, fauces, and uvula visible, but tonsillar pillars not seen

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes Mallampati Class II — generally not associated with difficult intubation.

answers.text: Soft palate and base of uvula only visible

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Mallampati Class III shows only the soft palate and base of the uvula — the fauces and tonsillar pillars are obscured, predicting a potentially difficult laryngoscopy.
Hard palate only visible is Mallampati Class IV — the most restricted view, strongly predicting difficult intubation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Mallampati Class III = soft palate + base of uvula only visible. Class I = full view; Class II = soft palate, fauces, uvula; Class IV = hard palate only.

Well done. Remember: Mallampati I–IV grades the oropharyngeal view (mouth opened, tongue protruded). It predicts glottic exposure difficulty, not overall anaesthetic risk (that is the ASA physical status).
